 Ford, Honda, Toyota Among Brands in Eight Vehicle Recalls
 Free Press Publisher 
 October 19, 2026 
 Lifestyle and Travel News , Notices 
 The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has listed eight recalls involving Ford, Ram, BMW, Toyota, Honda, Hyundai, Genesis and Volvo vehicles.
 A park-outside warning applies to certain 2015–2016 Hyundai Genesis and 2017–2020 Genesis G80 vehicles because overheated power seat motors may cause a fire. The recall number is 26V664.
 The other recalls include:
 2015 Ford Transit Connect: The rearview camera image may appear blank or distorted. Recall number: 26V650.
 2026 Ram 2500: Vehicles may lose electronic stability control, involving Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 126. Recall number: 26V651.
 2025–2027 Ford F-150: Front-row seats may be improperly secured. Recall number: 26V655.
 2021–2024 BMW R 18: The reverse gear control unit may overheat. Recall number: 26V658.
 2026 Toyota RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid: A motor generator electronic control unit error may cause a loss of drive power. Recall number: 26V659.
 2023–2026 Honda Accord Hybrid and CR-V Hybrid, and 2025 Honda CR-V Fuel Cell EV: The tire repair kit bottle cap may detach. Recall number: 26V663.
 2025–2026 Volvo EX30 and 2026 Volvo EX30CC: The head restraint cushion may detach. Recall number: 26V671.
 Owners can enter their license plate number or vehicle identification number in NHTSA’s recall lookup tool to determine whether their vehicle has an unrepaired recall. Owners of affected vehicles should contact their local dealership to schedule a free repair.

 The Franklin County Free Press, established by Vicky Taylor in 2019, emerged as a beacon of local journalism for the residents of Franklin County. Under Vicky's leadership, it quickly became an essential source of news, particularly at a time when major newspaper publications were increasingly overlooking local coverage. 
On January 1, 2022, the torch was passed to Nathan Neil and his firm, Neil Publishing, LLC. Neil, a local entrepreneur with multiple thriving businesses in Chambersburg, shares Vicky's fervent commitment to both the community and the world of local journalism. 
Rooted in the heart of Franklin County and powered by its residents, the Franklin County Free Press continues to bridge the gap, ensuring that the local stories, events, and issues that matter most to the community remain in the spotlight.
